requirements_summary: Enterprise ecommerce platform: customer-facing chat assistants (personalization and promotions), real-time reranking for product search, nightly embedding pipelines for catalog updates. Must guarantee <P95 latency 200ms for single-turn chat under sustained load, throughput 100-150 qps with bursts to 350. Cost sensitivity on embeddings; prefer higher utilization for cheaper per-embed cost. Data residency: US only. KMS required. Prefer reserved capacity with ability to scale burst to hosted in outage.
reserved_capacity_plan: Draft sizing (workshop outputs): Option A - Performance-first: 8 x H100 equivalents (dedicated pool) to meet latency and burst SLOs; target utilization 45% baseline, 75% peak -> commit 6 GPUs equiv. Option B - Cost-first: 20 x A100-80GB equiv for similar throughput at higher latency tail; commit 14 GPUs equiv. Proposal: 12-month commit for initial term, with quarterly utilization reassessments and ability to reallocate 2 GPUs between regions. Include 20% burst buffer from hosted pool. Needs explicit mapping table of model family -> preferred SKU (eg. Llama-3-70B quantized -> A100 recommended; Llama-3-13B -> H100 for p95).
cost_model_highlights: Commit tiers considered: 50% commit (lower monthly), 70% commit (better unit price), 90% commit (highest discount)
Assumed utilization bands: low 30% (night/weekend), baseline 45% (business hours), peak 75% (holiday or sale events)
Unit economics: modeled per-1k tokens across routes: chat gen $0.028--$0.042 per 1k tokens depending on model and SKU, embeddings $0.006--$0.012 per 1k tokens when batched overnight
Breakeven analysis: 12-mo 70% commit beats hosted for >120M tokens/month; 50% commit only cost-effective if embeddings >200M tokens/month or utilization spikes frequent
Sensitivity: +/-10% utilization shifts ARR by ~12% due to amortized GPU fixed cost
sla_negotiation_notes: Customer requests: 99.95% uptime for dedicated pool, p95 latency guarantee for chat route at <200ms with credits for SLO breaches. Legal: wants liability cap aligned to monthly committed spend. They asked for a 'performance appendix' detailing measurement points (edge vs. model host) and fallbacks. We proposed: SLA uptime 99.9% tier with credits ladder; separate performance SLO measured at Redwood edge with 2-minute sampling windows; automatic failover to hosted model variants with throttled QoS in case of full pool outage. Procurement to push for a 30-day performance remediation window before credits. SE notes: need to confirm observability hooks to provide per-route latency dashboards in Console for contract reporting.
